strings.name: Carolyn Bertozzi
strings.summary: Carolyn Bertozzi developed selective chemical reactions to study sugars on cell surfaces in complex biological environments. With her team she advanced bioorthogonal chemistry, allowing researchers to trace molecules while minimizing disruption of normal processes. The methods connect glycobiology, imaging and drug research. She shared the 2022 Nobel Prize in Chemistry with Barry Sharpless and Morten Meldal.

strings.highlights.highlight-1.title: Bioorthogonal reactions
strings.highlights.highlight-1.text: Developed reactions selective enough for biological settings, helping label and observe otherwise difficult molecular targets.
strings.highlights.highlight-2.title: Cell-surface sugars
strings.highlights.highlight-2.text: Investigates how glycans contribute to cellular communication and disease, applying chemical tools to imaging and therapeutic candidates.
